correctness.rationale: A total dominating edge set in K_n is characterized exactly by at most one isolate and no two-vertex component. Inclusion minimality removes all cycles, forces P3 components in the isolate-free case, and forces every nonpendant component edge to split off K2 when there is one isolate. The core-tree argument characterizes precisely the allowed spiders; the only multiple-hub enumeration is the 4-vertex path, corrected by -z³u⁴/2. The labeled component exponential formula proves all coefficients and extrema for n≥3. A standalone exact brute-force checker independently enumerates 2,131,016 candidate subsets for n=3..7, with complete coefficient agreement. Finite checks support but do not replace the general proof.

originality.rationale: The closest relevant primary works give (i) upper-total-domination bounds for claw-free graphs, (ii) a general open-neighborhood transversal enumeration equivalence, (iii) a polynomial-delay algorithm for ORDINARY edge domination using closed neighborhoods, and (iv) an all-total-dominating-set polynomial. Their mathematical statements do not imply an explicit classification and exact cardinality enumerator of inclusion-minimal TOTAL domination in L(K_n). Published-record and alias/implication searches returned no stronger exact coverage; this is not claimed to prove global priority. Inaccessible full texts and renaming risks remain explicit.
residual_risks: No exhaustive literature search can certify novelty; an equivalent complete enumeration under total-edge domination, open-neighborhood hitting sets, or another graph name might exist.
Full text of Favaron–Henning (2003) was not accessible after open-access attempts; its abstract concerns broad extremal bounds, but its possible detailed special cases remain unknown.
The complete 2014 total-domination-polynomial article was gated, although its definition enumerates all sets rather than minimal sets.
Self-review is not independent validation. Exhaustive experiments cover only n=3..7.

value.rationale: The family is a standard claw-free, highly symmetric line-graph family. Counting all inclusion-minimal total dominating sets is substantively different from merely evaluating the classical minimum number: it determines the entire minimal-object size distribution and the upper total-domination parameter. The one-isolate spider dichotomy is structural; the hub ambiguity correction and labeled EGF yield an exact reusable description, not an arbitrary finite census or a substitution into a known tabulation.
